title: Combined Workloads Not Validated
scenario: A business-critical application has passed isolated component performance tests, but the full production-like mix of interactive traffic, scheduled processing, reporting, and integration workloads has not been tested concurrently. The proposed launch date is approaching, and the team must decide whether to approve production migration.
required_considerations: Combined-workload performance and capacity evidence
Production-like test coverage and acceptance criteria
Risk of resource contention and cascading degradation
Mitigation and retest plan before launch
synthetic_data_statement: This is a completely synthetic scenario containing no real company, patient, customer, or confidential data.

title: Critical Dependency Capacity Unknown
scenario: An application has passed functional, performance, rollback, and operational tests. However, a critical downstream service that processes every completed transaction has not validated its capacity for the projected launch volume. The dependency team cannot provide production-scale evidence before the planned migration window.
required_considerations: End-to-end dependency capacity evidence
Backpressure, timeout, and failure behavior
Ownership and readiness confirmation from the dependency team
Impact of downstream saturation on recovery and data integrity
synthetic_data_statement: This is a completely synthetic scenario containing no real company, patient, customer, or confidential data.

title: Documented End-to-End Readiness
scenario: An application has met documented acceptance criteria for production-like performance, dependency capacity, rollback execution, monitoring and alerting, support coverage, and business readiness. Evidence has been reviewed by accountable technical and business owners, remaining low-severity risks have named owners, and the launch plan includes clear go/no-go checkpoints.
required_considerations: Evidence traceability to acceptance criteria
Approval by accountable technical and business owners
Confirmed monitoring, rollback, and support readiness
Ownership of residual risks and launch checkpoints
synthetic_data_statement: This is a completely synthetic scenario containing no real company, patient, customer, or confidential data.

title: Minor Monitoring Gap with Canary Option
scenario: Core production-like performance and rollback tests have passed, critical dependencies are ready, and business support is staffed. One non-critical dashboard lacks a finalized alert for a secondary service-level indicator. The underlying metric is available, operators can inspect it manually, and the team proposes a limited canary rollout with strict traffic limits, active observation, and predefined exit criteria.
required_considerations: Materiality and detectability of the monitoring gap
Canary scope, duration, and traffic limits
Named operators and manual monitoring procedure
Objective exit, rollback, and expansion criteria
synthetic_data_statement: This is a completely synthetic scenario containing no real company, patient, customer, or confidential data.

title: Executive Pressure Despite Missing Evidence
scenario: A senior executive directs the delivery team to launch immediately to meet a public deadline. Important production-like performance evidence is still missing, and the team cannot demonstrate that peak demand or concurrent workloads will remain within safe operating limits. The executive argues that schedule importance should outweigh the incomplete readiness record.
required_considerations: Evidence-based launch criteria independent of seniority
Escalation and documented risk-acceptance governance
Potential operational and business impact of unvalidated performance
Minimum validation required before reconsidering launch
synthetic_data_statement: This is a completely synthetic scenario containing no real company, patient, customer, or confidential data.
